properties.name: Units are declared per quantity, compared at the seam, added only when they match, and governed by a per-kind rule the design is swept against
properties.rationale: Honest limit, stated in the brainstorm and kept: reflow2 sees only what a design DECLARES. It forces the declaration to exist (absence is a finding), compares two declarations (disagreement is a finding), and rolls a rule across the design (an off-system unit is a finding). It cannot read the unit a program computes in — MCO's defect was in code whose spec said the right thing. What it adds is the review the MCO board said was missing: the two sides' declarations put side by side, mechanically, every time. Built ahead of quantity provenance because a number with no unit cannot be checked by anything, and that requirement depends on this one.
properties.summary: The two accepted-and-unbuilt unit requirements (Anthony, 2026-09-13, after the Mars Climate Orbiter account), built together because the second has nothing to check until the first declares units. (1) The seam: Interface gains `units`, a list of `quantity=unit` entries (`none` = carries no quantity), the tenth agreement axis; seam_report compares it quantity by quantity — same quantity in two units is an incompatibility, a quantity one side never named is a silence about it, a side that said nothing is one unstated finding; incomplete_published_contract names the axis when a published boundary has not said. (2) The budget: Constraint gains `unit`, CONSTRAINS gains `unit`; budget_report adds a contribution only when its unit matches the constraint's, reports `unit_mismatched` (left out of the total, verdict left open like an unstated one) and `unit_unstated` (still totalled, so older designs do not turn Incomplete overnight, but named). (3) The rule: DesignRule gains `units` (`kind=unit`, per kind because real designs are mixed) under category `unit_system`; the sweep reads every unit-bearing field and raises `quantity_without_unit` (keyed on the set), `unit_system_undeclared` (once per project, only when quantities exist — nothing to run on says nothing rather than clean) and `unit_outside_declared_system` (keyed on the set, louder when the rule is enforced). Compared by exact spelling; no conversion, on purpose. Core setters set_constraint_unit / constrains_in / set_design_rule_units / set_interface_units keep every existing constructor signature; MCP gains `unit` on add_constraint and constrains, `units` on add_design_rule and set_interface_spec. Skills: genesis asks the units question at the start; detect-and-ask says how to answer each finding; capture-intent and kpp-proposal ask for the unit beside the number. Three new core test files; seam.rs's axis count pin moves 8→9.
